title: Senator Tan Parker criticizes bond process after Texas Capitol plot suspect re-arrested
text:
← Back to the wire
Senator Tan Parker criticizes bond process after Texas Capitol plot suspect re-arrested
Senator Tan Parker posted several updates on October 1, 2026 regarding the arrest and quick release of a suspect accused of plotting an attack on the Texas Capitol.
Senator Tan Parker, a Republican representing Texas's 12th Senate district, used his social media platform on October 1, 2026, to comment on the arrest and subsequent release of a man accused of plotting an attack on the Texas Capitol.
In his first post, Parker wrote: "Let me get this straight: a man accused of plotting an attack on the Texas Capitol, with a prior weapons charge, was arrested at 3 a.m. and bonded out the same morning. $75,000? That's a joke. This man is a danger to every Texan who walks through those doors and to communities" (October 1, 2026).
Later that morning, Parker provided an update about the case: "UPDATE: That $75K bond didn't get him far. Thankfully, he's back in custody on a federal warrant. Thank you to our @TxDPS heroes for putting in the extra work with our federal partners to keep him behind bars where he belongs. Next session, I'm filing legislation to slam this https://t.co/57pI8Jbi0C" (October 1, 2026).
Parker has represented Texas's 12th Senate district since his election in 2023 and succeeded Angela Paxton as state senator.
